The three proposed answers are N, N, and N(N−1)/2. I could not verify the reference result, and my recollection of the literature is not reliable enough to confirm a specific formula. Working from the structure of the problem, none of the three looks correct.

- **Solution 3 (N(N−1)/2)** gives 0 poles at N = 1. A single algebraic soliton has a denominator that is a quadratic with complex-conjugate roots, which places one pole in the upper half-plane. Its pairwise-interaction reasoning is asserted rather than derived.
- **Solutions 1 and 2 (N)** get the N = 1 case right but do not account for the interaction poles that the double-Wronskian tau function carries at higher N. Their justification is also thin: Solution 1 assumes each soliton contributes a single pole with no argument for why, and Solution 2 asserts that no interaction poles persist.

A count consistent with the N = 1 case and with the double-Wronskian degree structure would be N(N+1)/2. I have not verified this, so I am not selecting it as a solution.

CHOICE: NONE
CONFIDENCE: 2
